summary: 澳洲野犬会捕食家畜，却也可能抑制威胁本土哺乳动物的狐狸和野猫。文章结合引入物种的历史、围栏两侧的差异及牧场经验，呈现保护生物多样性与减少牲畜损失之间的争议。

paragraphs.brief: 一架飞机在澳大利亚西北部金伯利地区的3,600平方公里长的农场卡尔顿希尔站上飞行缓慢。
sentences: A plane flies a slow pattern over Carlton Hill station, a 3,600 square kilometre ranch in the Kimberley region in northwest Australia.
一架飞机在澳大利亚西北部金伯利地区的3,600平方公里长的农场卡尔顿希尔站上飞行缓慢。
As the plane circles, those aboard drop 1,000 small pieces of meat, one by one, onto the scrubland below, each piece laced with poison; this practice is known as baiting.
当飞机绕圈时，机上的人将1000块肉一个一个扔到下面的洗涤场上，每一块都带了毒药，这被称为诱饵。
Besides 50,000 head of cattle, Carlton Hill is home to the dingo, Australia’s largest mammalian predator and the bane of a grazier’s (cattle farmer’s) life.
除了5万头牛卡尔顿山是澳大利亚最大的哺乳动物捕食者和牛群农夫的家园
Stuart McKechnie, manager of Carlton Hill, complains that graziers’ livelihoods are threatened when dingoes prey on cattle.
卡尔顿山的经理斯图尔特·麦基奇尼抱怨说，在猎杀牛时，疯人的生活受到威胁。
But one man wants the baiting to end, and for dingoes to once again roam Australia’s wide-open spaces.
但有一个人想结束诱饵，并让独木舟再次游荡澳大利亚的宽阔空间。
According to Chris Johnson of James Cook University, “Australia needs more dingoes to protect our biodiversity.”
根据詹姆斯·库克大学的Chris Johnson所说，“澳大利亚需要更多鸽子来保护我们的生物多样性。”

paragraphs.brief: 大约4000年前，亚洲水手们向澳大利亚引进了单艇
sentences: About 4,000 years ago, Asian sailors introduced dingoes to Australia.
大约4000年前，亚洲水手们向澳大利亚引进了单艇

Throughout the ensuing millennia, these descendants of the wolf spread across the continent and, as the Tasmanian tiger disappeared completely from Australia, dingoes became Australia’s top predators.
在接下来的千年中，狼的后代遍布整个大陆，随着塔斯马尼亚老虎从澳大利亚完全消失，小鹦鹉成为澳大利亚最大的掠食动物。
As agricultural development took place, the European settlers found that they could not safely keep their livestock where dingoes roamed.
随着农业发展的开展，欧洲定居者发现，他们无法安全地将牲畜存放在独木舟漫游的地方。
So began one of the most sustained efforts at pest control in Australia’s history.
因此开始在澳大利亚历史上最持久的虫害防治努力之一。
Over the last 150 years, dingoes have been shot and poisoned, and fences have been used in an attempt to keep them away from livestock.
过去150年来，独眼鹦鹉遭到枪击和毒害，并使用栅栏试图使他们远离牲畜。
But at the same time, as the European settlers tried to eliminate one native pest from Australia, they introduced more of their own.
但与此同时，当欧洲定居者试图从澳大利亚消灭一种本地害虫时，他们引入了更多的自己的害虫。

paragraphs.brief: 兔子数量在减少 — — 并且除了本地哺乳动物外，狐狸和猫群数量仍然减少，但数量仍然很大。
sentences: In 1860, the rabbit was unleashed on Australia by a wealthy landowner and by 1980 rabbits had covered most of the mainland.
1860年，一只兔子被一个富有的地主释放到澳大利亚，到1980年，兔子覆盖了大部分大陆。
Rabbits provide huge prey base for two other introduced species: the feral (wild) cat and the red fox.
兔子为另外两种引进的物种提供了巨大的猎物基地：野猫和红狐。
The interaction between foxes, cats and rabbits is a huge problem for native mammals.
狐狸、猫和兔子之间的相互作用对本地哺乳动物来说是个大问题
In good years, rabbit numbers increase dramatically, and fox and cat populations grow quickly in response to the abundance of this prey.
在好年头里，兔子的数量急剧增加狐狸和猫群也迅速增长以适应这种猎物的丰量
When bad seasons follow, rabbit numbers are significantly reduced – and the dwindling but still large fox and cat populations are left with little to eat besides native mammals.
兔子数量在减少 — — 并且除了本地哺乳动物外，狐狸和猫群数量仍然减少，但数量仍然很大。

paragraphs.brief: 澳大利亚哺乳动物通常比兔子、猫和狐狸繁殖得慢得多 — — 这是一种适应性，以防止干旱环境中的过度人口，因为那里的粮食可能稀缺和不可靠 — — 并且人口减少，因为它们的生长速度不足以替代被食肉动物杀死的动物。
sentences: Australian mammals generally reproduce much more slowly than rabbits, cats and foxes – an adaption to prevent overpopulation in the arid environment, where food can be scarce and unreliable – and populations decline because they can’t grow fast enough to replace animals killed by the predators.
澳大利亚哺乳动物通常比兔子、猫和狐狸繁殖得慢得多 — — 这是一种适应性，以防止干旱环境中的过度人口，因为那里的粮食可能稀缺和不可靠 — — 并且人口减少，因为它们的生长速度不足以替代被食肉动物杀死的动物。
Johnson says dingoes are the solution to this problem because they keep cat and fox populations under control.
强生说独木舟是解决这个问题的办法因为它们控制着猫和狐狸种群
Besides regularly eating the smaller predators, dingoes will kill them simply to lessen competition.
除了经常吃小捕食者外鱼会杀死它们只是为了减少竞争
Dingo packs live in large, stable territories and generally have only one fertile female, which limits their rate of increase.
迪尼戈人生活在大而稳定的土地上，一般只有一名育龄妇女，这限制了她们的增长率。
In the 4,000 years that dingoes have been Australia, they have contributed to few, if any, extinctions, Johnson says.
Johnson说，它们导致的灭绝，如果有的话，也很少：“在4000年里独木舟是澳大利亚。”

paragraphs.brief: 实际上，澳大利亚是一个由这些动物主导的国家 - - 2500万牛，10000万羊，还有20多万人。
sentences: Reaching out from a desolate spot where three states meet, for 2,500 km in either direction, is the world’s longest fence, two meters high and stretching from the coast in Queensland to the Great Australian Bight in South Australia; it is there to keep dingoes out of southeast, the fence separates the main types of livestock found in Australia.
距离三个州的荒凉地处，在两条方向上，长达2,500公里，是世界上最长的围，高2米，从昆士兰海岸延伸到南澳大利亚的大澳大利亚湾，它是为了让鱼远离东南部，围隔离了澳大利亚主要的牲畜。
To the northwest of the fence, cattle predominate; to the southwest, sheep fill the landscape.
在栅栏西北，牛占多数；在西南，羊占地势。
In fact, Australia is a land dominated by these animals – 25 million cattle, 100 million sheep and just over 20 million people.
实际上，澳大利亚是一个由这些动物主导的国家 - - 2500万牛，10000万羊，还有20多万人。

paragraphs.brief: 在他们的研究中，一些最大的幼崽掠夺率发生在被诱骗的地区。
sentences: While there is no argument that dingoes will prey on sheep if given the chance, they don’t hunt cattle once the calves are much past two or three weeks old, according to McKechnie.
麦肯尼认为，虽然没有争论说，如果有机会，小鹦鹉会猎食羊，但幼崽已经超过两三个星期了，它们不会猎杀牛。
And a study in Queensland suggests that dingoes don’t even prey heavily on the newborn calves unless their staple prey disappears due to deteriorating conditions like drought.
昆士兰的一项研究表明，只鹦鹉甚至不会大量猎食新生幼崽，除非它们的主食因干旱等不断恶化的状况而消失。

This study, co-authored by Lee Allen of the Robert Wicks Research Centre in Queensland, suggests that the aggressive baiting programs used against dingoes may actually be counter-productive for graziers.
这项由昆士兰Robert Wicks研究中心的Lee Allen共同撰写的研究报告表明，针对单艇的侵略性诱饵方案实际上可能会对食人者产生反作用。
When dingoes are removed from an area by baiting, the area is recolonized by younger, more solitary dingoes.
当用诱饵把独木舟从一个区域移走时，这个区域被更年轻、更孤独的独木舟重新殖民。
These animals aren’t capable of going after large prey like kangaroos, so they turn to calves.
这些动物无法捕捉像袋鼠这样的大猎物，所以它们变成了小牛。
In their study, some of the highest rates of calf predation occurred in areas that had been baited.
在他们的研究中，一些最大的幼崽掠夺率发生在被诱骗的地区。

paragraphs.brief: 也不相信小鹦鹉的生态利益，说他不相信它们能捕到猫，认为它们更可能捕到小的当地动物。
sentences: Mark Clifford, general manager of a firm that manages over 200,000 head of cattle, is not convinced by Allen’s assertion.
Mark Clifford，一家管理20多万头牛的公司的总经理并不相信艾伦的说法。
Clifford says, “It’s obvious if we drop or loosen control on dingoes, we are going to lose more calves.”
克里夫德说：“ 如果我们放弃或放松对独木舟的控制，我们就会失去更多的小牛。”
He doesn’t believe that dingoes will go after kangaroos when calves are around.
他不相信幼崽在附近时，独木舟会追逐袋鼠。

Nor is he persuaded of dingoes’ supposed ecological benefits, saying he is not convinced that they manage to catch cats that often, believing they are more likely to catch small native animals instead.
也不相信小鹦鹉的生态利益，说他不相信它们能捕到猫，认为它们更可能捕到小的当地动物。

paragraphs.brief: 麦克奇尼认同澳洲野犬会捕杀与他的牛争夺食物的沙袋鼠（一种当地的小型动物）。但他也指出，西澳大利亚州部分地区没有狐狸，猫的数量也不多。
sentences: McKechnie agrees that dingoes kill the wallabies (small native animals) that compete with his cattle for food, but points out that in parts of Western Australia, there are no foxes, and not very many cats.
麦克奇尼认同澳洲野犬会捕杀与他的牛争夺食物的沙袋鼠（一种当地的小型动物）。但他也指出，西澳大利亚州部分地区没有狐狸，猫的数量也不多。
He doesn’t see how relaxing controls on dingoes in his area will improve the ecological balance.
他不明白放松对甲壳类动物的控制会如何改善生态平衡。
Johnson sees a need for a change in philosophy on the part of graziers.
约翰逊认为需要改变思想的偏执者。
“There might be a number of different ways of thinking through dingo management in cattle country,” he says.
“在牛群国家，通过dingo管理，可能有多种不同的思维方式”。
“At the moment, though, that hasn’t got through to graziers.
不过目前还不能让那些疯子知道
There’s still just one prescription, and that is to bait as widely as possible.”
” ”但只有一个处方，即尽可能广泛地诱饵。

items.en: a description of a barrier designed to stop dingoes, which also divides two kinds of non-natives animals
items.zh: 描述一个旨在停止独木舟的屏障，该屏障还分割两种非本地动物
items.why: 描述了2 500 km长的栅栏，既阻挡野狗，又把两种外来经济动物一牛和羊-一分隔在两侧。

items.en: how dingoes ensure that rival species do not dominate
items.zh: 独木舟如何确保竞争的物种不会占优势
items.why: 说明野狗通过捕食甚至“竞争性捕杀” 猫、狐来防止竞争物种数量过大。

items.en: a reference to a widespread non-native species that other animals feed on
items.zh: 指其他动物所食用的广泛的非本地物种。
items.why: 提到遍布全国的外来物种"兔子",并点出猫、狐狸依赖其为食。

items.en: a mention of the dingo’s arrival in Australia
items.why: B段给出野犬抵澳的时间和途径，约四千年前由亚洲海员引入。

items.en: research which has proved that dingoes have resorted to eating young livestock
items.zh: 研究证明独木舟已经使用食用年轻的牲畜
items.why: Lee Allen 的研究发现: 被诱杀后返巢的年轻野狗捕食小牛竺，表明野狗开始吃幼年家畜。

items.en: a description of a method used to kill dingoes
items.zh: 描述用于杀独眼鹦鹉的方法
items.why: 详细描述了飞机投放毒肉诱杀 (baiting) 的方法。

items.en: the way that the structure of dingo groups affects how quickly their numbers grow
items.zh: 丁戈人的结构影响他们人数的迅速增长
items.why: 解释了群体结构 (仅一只可繁殖雌性) 如何限制种群增长速度。

items.en: Dingoes tend to hunt native animals rather than hunting other non-native predators.
items.zh: 独目动物往往猎杀本地动物，而不是猎杀其他非本地捕食者。

items.en: The presence of dingoes puts the income of some people at risk.
items.zh: 独木舟的存在使一些人的收入处于危险之中。

items.en: Dingoes have had little impact on the dying out of animal species in Australia.
items.zh: 丁戈鱼对澳大利亚动物物种的灭绝影响甚微。

items.en: The dingo replaced the ________as the main predatory animal in Australia.
items.zh: 澳洲野犬取代了________，成为澳大利亚主要的捕食者。
items.why: 说明袋狼消失后由野狗取代其顶级捕食者地位。

items.en: Foxes and cats are more likely to hunt native animals when there are fewer________
items.zh: 当________的数量变少时，狐狸和猫更可能捕食本土动物。
items.why: 当免子数量下降时，狐与猫更倾向捕食本土动物。

items.en: Australian animals reproduce at a slow rate as a natural way of avoiding ________
items.zh: 澳大利亚动物繁殖较慢，这是一种自然避免________的方式。
items.why: 慢速繁殖是一种避免“过度繁殖”(overpopulation) 的自然适应。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

pairs: a barrier designed to stop dingoes
题干通过用途描述围栏。原文的 keep out 指把澳洲野犬挡在外面。
puts the income of some people at risk
题干说收入面临风险，原文具体写放牧者的生计受到威胁。
the dying out of animal species
动词短语 die out 在原文中变成名词 extinction，都指物种灭绝。
points: 说明野狗通过捕食甚至“竞争性捕杀” 猫、狐来防止竞争物种数量过大。
慢速繁殖是一种避免“过度繁殖”(overpopulation) 的自然适应。
clauses: Stuart McKechnie, manager of Carlton Hill, complains ….
“that graziers’ livelihoods are threatened when dingoes prey on cattle”补足 complains 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 complains 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

Australian mammals generally reproduce much more slowly than rabbits, cats and foxes – an adaption to prevent overpopulation in the arid environment, where food can be scarce and unreliable – and populations decline ….
连接词 because 引出“because they can’t grow fast enough to replace animals killed by the predators”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Graziers see them as pests, and poisoning is common, but some biologists think Australia’s dingoes are the best weapon in a war against imported cats and foxes.
但一些生物学家认为澳大利亚的独木舟是针对进口猫和狐狸的最好武器。
